name: Sodium Bicarbonate
description: Fine white powder, softer and finer than salt. Also known as baking soda.

clues.text: Doesn't catch fire, and barely changes the flame's color at all.
Mildly basic -- turns the litmus paper faintly blue, around pH 8-9.
Dissolves completely in water, leaving a clear liquid.
Fizzes and bubbles the moment vinegar touches it -- that's carbon dioxide gas escaping!
No smell at all.

name: Sodium Chloride
description: Small clear-white crystals, coarser than baking soda. The stuff sprinkled on fries.

clues.text: Burns with a bright, intense yellow-orange flame -- that's the sodium inside it.
Neutral -- doesn't change the litmus paper at all, right around pH 7.
Dissolves completely in water, leaving a clear liquid.
No reaction with vinegar -- it stays exactly the same.
No smell at all.

name: Calcium Carbonate
description: A chalky white solid that doesn't dissolve easily -- the same mineral found in seashells and limestone.

clues.text: Burns with a faint brick-red-orange tint -- that's the calcium inside it.
Mildly basic -- turns the litmus paper faintly blue.
Barely dissolves in water -- most of it sinks and stays solid.
Fizzes and bubbles with vinegar, just like baking soda does.
No smell at all.

name: Citric Acid
description: Small, sharp-looking white crystals -- the sour taste behind lemons and lemonade powder.

clues.text: Chars and blackens instead of burning cleanly -- a sign it's built from carbon, like sugar.
Strongly acidic -- turns the litmus paper red, down around pH 2-3.
Dissolves completely in water, leaving a clear, sour-tasting liquid.
No fizzing with vinegar -- two acids meeting doesn't make gas. It's the OTHER acid that makes baking soda fizz.
No strong smell, but unmistakably sour to taste.

name: Sugar
description: Small clear-white crystals that taste sweet -- the same stuff in a kitchen sugar bowl.

clues.text: Melts, browns, and chars -- caramelizing before it ever really catches fire.
Neutral -- doesn't change the litmus paper at all.
Dissolves completely in water, leaving a clear, sweet-tasting liquid.
No reaction with vinegar -- it stays exactly the same.
No smell at all, but unmistakably sweet to taste.

name: Epsom Salt
description: Small colorless crystals, often dissolved in warm baths to soothe sore muscles.

clues.text: Burns with almost no change to the flame's color.
Close to neutral, maybe just a touch acidic -- right around pH 6-7.
Dissolves completely in water, leaving a clear liquid.
No fizzing or bubbling with vinegar.
No smell at all.
